## Purpose and status

Agreed on 23 September 2026. This case provides the common wind-farm and
onshore hydrogen-delivery basis for the centralised and turbine-level
comparisons. It is an idealised case based on IJmuiden Ver Beta, not a claim to
reproduce the developer's final design.

The authoritative article inputs are in
[reference_case.toml](scenarios/reference_case.toml). Values displayed here are
loaded from that record; dimensions and spacing are calculated by
[the reference-case calculation](analysis/reference_case.py). These are case
choices, not defaults for the component methodology. The architecture templates
have not yet been connected to this record: this note records the agreed basis,
not a completed production or cost run. Remaining preparation is tracked in
[O1](OPEN_POINTS.md).

## Common inputs and their basis

| Quantity | Adopted value | Classification, evidence and reason |
|---|---|---|
| Reference site and approximate location | IJmuiden Ver Beta; {{< var ijv-latitude-deg-n >}}° N, {{< var ijv-longitude-deg-e >}}° E | Sourced location in the RVO wake study, Appendix A [@rvo2025WakeStudy]. Identifies the geographical reference; it does not identify the supplied DOWA extraction point. |
| Turbine count $N$ | {{< var ijv-turbine-count >}} turbines | Article choice, matching the reference configuration in the same study [@rvo2025WakeStudy]. Keeps the upstream farm identical in both architectures. |
| Turbine rating $P_r$ | {{< var ijv-rated-power-mw >}} MW/turbine | Article choice, matching that reference configuration [@rvo2025WakeStudy]. Rating alone does not select a rotor, hub height or performance curve. |
| Net farm area $A$ | {{< var ijv-farm-area-km2 >}} km² | Sourced from the final Beta site decision, §4.2.1 [@ijmuidenBeta2023SiteDecision]. Uses Beta's net area rather than the area of the wider wind zone. It sets the equivalent rectangular layout and the denominator for yield per **net** km². |
| Representative water depth $h$ | {{< var ijv-water-depth-m >}} m | Sourced average for Beta in DNV's RVO assessment, Appendix B, Table 3 [@dnv2025Doordewind]. A published site-specific average is sufficient for this common structural and installation reference. It does not resolve local bathymetry, tides or a foundation design datum. |
| Crosswind breadth / along-wind length $r$ | {{< var ijv-crosswind-to-alongwind-ratio >}} | Explicit article assumption agreed on the date above. Represents the requested broad front perpendicular to the dominant wind. |
| Hydrogen export route | {{< var ijv-export-length-km >}} km | Explicit article assumption agreed on the date above. Physical route length from the offshore export origin to the common onshore receipt boundary; no surveyed pipeline corridor is claimed. |
| Onshore delivery pressure $p_{\mathrm{delivery,g}}$ | {{< var ijv-delivery-pressure-bar-g >}} bar(g) | Article choice based on the upper network-pressure level described for Waterstofnetwerk West-Nederland [@hynetwork2026WestNRD, p. 18]. The **gauge** interpretation is explicitly agreed modelling judgement; that source writes only “bar”. |
| Electrolyser stack outlet pressure $p_{\mathrm{stack,g}}$ | {{< var ijv-stack-outlet-pressure-bar-g >}} bar(g) | User-specified article assumption, applied to the centralised and turbine-level stacks alike. The **gauge** interpretation follows the delivery-pressure convention. It sets the compressor inlet pressure; it is not a product qualification of the supplied stack curve, whose source material reports approximately 30 bar ([Stack](../../hydrogen_production/stack.qmd)). |
| Stack overplant factor $f$ | {{< var ijv-overplant-factor >}}× baseline; up to {{< var ijv-overplant-factor-sensitivity-max >}}× later | Explicit article choices, applied equally to both architectures. Establish the baseline before investigating the additional stack-capacity trade-off. |

The installed wind capacity is derived, not independently prescribed:

$$
P_{\mathrm{farm}}=N P_r.
$$

Here $P_{\mathrm{farm}}$ is in MW, $N$ is a turbine count and $P_r$ is in
MW/turbine. The result is **{{< var ijv-installed-mw >}} MW**. “Approximately
2 GW” is a descriptive label; calculations retain the exact count-times-rating
result without introducing an electricity-grid export cap.

## Layout and spacing derived from area

Let $B$ be crosswind breadth and $L$ along-wind length, both in km. With
$A$ in km² and dimensionless $r=B/L$:

$$
B=\sqrt{Ar},\qquad L=\sqrt{A/r},\qquad BL=A.
$$

This gives **{{< var ijv-breadth-km >}} km across the wind** and
**{{< var ijv-length-km >}} km along the wind**. The adopted regular-grid
construction chooses the number of crosswind columns $n_B$ and along-wind rows
$n_L$ as:

$$
n_B=\left\lceil\sqrt{Nr}\right\rceil,\qquad
n_L=\left\lceil N/n_B\right\rceil.
$$

The resulting grid has {{< var ijv-columns >}} columns and
{{< var ijv-rows >}} rows: {{< var ijv-full-rows >}} full rows and a centred
final row of {{< var ijv-last-row >}} turbines. This row convention is an
explicit modelling choice; area and aspect ratio alone do not uniquely define
a turbine layout.

Turbine centres span the equivalent rectangle, with no additional boundary
setback. Consequently, the separations in metres are:

$$
d_B=\frac{1000B}{n_B-1},\qquad
d_L=\frac{1000L}{n_L-1}.
$$

The factor 1000 converts km to m. Crosswind spacing is
**{{< var ijv-spacing-crosswind-m >}} m** and along-wind spacing is
**{{< var ijv-spacing-alongwind-m >}} m**. The shorter final row retains $d_B$
and is centred within the same breadth. All wake and collection calculations
must use the resulting common turbine coordinates, rather than a separate
area-based spacing proxy.

Replacing the net site by a rectangle deliberately omits its actual shape,
internal corridors and exclusions. This is a comparative layout, not a
demonstration of site-permit compliance. Detailed polygon checks remain D7.

## Wind record and orientation

Use the supplied DOWA-derived hourly workbook and fitted sector table already
described on [Wind Resource and Weibull Distribution](../../wind_resource_and_layout/wind_resource_and_weibull.qmd).
Their paths are recorded in the case file. DOWA is the underlying atlas
[@dutchOffshoreWindAtlas]; the atlas citation does not independently establish
the workbook's extraction point or height. Retain the page's existing metadata
and period limitations without substituting an unrelated wind record.

The adopted orientation follows the centre of the most frequent direction
sector in the supplied table: **{{< var ijv-dominant-from-deg >}}°**, interpreted
as the meteorological direction **from** which wind arrives, clockwise from
north. Thus the short axis runs southwest–northeast and the long axis
northwest–southeast. Sector labels in the existing file are lower bin edges;
use bin centres when preparing wake states. The centre is calculated from the
stored sector spacing rather than entered as another independent case value.

This documents the adopted interpretation. It does not recover the missing
direction-convention metadata for the original extraction. Both architectures
must receive identical annual wind-state weights and turbine-level generation
before architecture-specific losses.

## Export and onshore delivery boundary

The reported product is hydrogen delivered at the common onshore receipt
interface at the adopted pressure. Include the export pipeline, landfall and
receipt functions needed to reach that boundary; exclude subsequent backbone
transport, storage, distribution and end use. The receipt equipment scope and
its supply, installation and operating costs remain O9.

The agreed export length is a scenario assumption. For context, the published
Beta electricity-connection assessment gives a **146 km offshore cable route**
toward Maasvlakte [@ijmuidenBeta2021ExportMER, Table 2-14, p. 67]. This is route
evidence for a different carrier, not an adopted hydrogen-pipeline length.
A particular landfall and engineered route remain unresolved.

The West-Netherlands hydrogen-network document describes initial operation at
**30–50 bar** and possible future operation up to **66 bar**
[@hynetwork2026WestNRD, p. 18]. Those are source-reported network conditions;
the article deliberately adopts the upper level as its delivery requirement.
It does not claim that every connection currently requires that pressure.

Compression and pipeline equations use **absolute** pressure. The agreed
delivery and stack outlet pressures are gauge values and are converted once, at
the model boundary:

$$
p_{\mathrm{abs}}=p_{\mathrm{g}}+p_{\mathrm{atm}}.
$$

All pressures in this equation are in bar. The atmospheric basis
$p_{\mathrm{atm}}$ is the standard atmosphere,
{{< var standard-atmospheric-pressure >}} (exactly 101 325 Pa
[@nist2008SP811]), applied at both the offshore stack outlet and the onshore
receipt boundary. This is an explicit modelling assumption: both points are
near sea level, and weather-driven barometric variation, of the order of a few
hundredths of a bar, is not modelled.

The result is a delivery pressure of
**{{< var ijv-delivery-pressure-bar-a >}} bar(a)** and a stack outlet pressure
of **{{< var ijv-stack-outlet-pressure-bar-a >}} bar(a)**, calculated by
[the reference-case calculation](analysis/reference_case.py). Scenario inputs
take these absolute values; the gauge values are never copied into an
absolute-pressure field. Any pressure loss through
receipt equipment belongs upstream of the delivery interface and must be
accounted for explicitly rather than hidden in a pressure margin.

## Stack sizing and comparison cases

Define the dimensionless overplant factor as:

$$
f=\frac{P_{\mathrm{stack,requested}}}{P_{\mathrm{wind,served}}},
$$

where both capacities are in MW at their stated rating boundaries. Central
stacks serve the complete farm; each turbine-level package serves its turbine.
Actual installed stack capacity follows the model's integer module sizing.
Overplanting changes stack capacity; it does not automatically increase the
wind rating or BOP design capacity. Operation must still cover auxiliary loads
within available wind power.

Start both architectures at the agreed baseline factor. Retain the agreed
upper factor for deferred sensitivity work (D6), not as a demonstrated feasible
design or an optimised result. Preserve the article's centralised, conservative
turbine-level and converter-reduced comparison cases; electrical equipment and
efficiency choices remain O2.

## Remaining preparation

**O1 is partially resolved.** The site, count/rating, area, schematic geometry,
representative depth, wind-data basis, export distance, delivery-pressure
and stack-outlet pressure interpretations and overplanting range are agreed. Before claiming executable
common-case results:

- Connect this shared record to both scenario templates and generate the common
  coordinates, including an explicit coordinate-rotation convention.
- Select a consistent rotor diameter, hub height and tabulated power/thrust
  curve; the nominal turbine rating alone does not supply these.
- Prepare annual operating states and peak-duty states from the existing wind
  data, using the documented sector-centre convention.
- Pass the converted absolute pressures to both templates and complete the
  remaining design inputs needed by the selected branches. Collection origins and network design are
  linked to O3/O7; onshore receipt details remain O9.
